newsitem.title: GERMANY: Institutes say Germany to miss Maastricht target.
newsitem.headline: Institutes say Germany to miss Maastricht target.

text.p: Six leading research institutes said on Tuesday Germany would fail to meet in 1997 the Maastricht criteria for the single European currency because its public-sector deficit was likely to be 3.5 percent of economic output.

The Maastricht Treaty says countries participating in European monetary union (EMU) must reduce their budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), and 1997 is the key year for deciding what countries will participate at the start of EMU, slated for January 1999.

In a semi-annual report due for release later on Tuesday, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, the six institutes said German GDP was likely to grow 1.5 pct in 1996, rising to 2.5 percent growth in 1997.

The report said Germany's total public sector deficit is likely to fall 17 billion marks to 127 billion marks in 1997 as the rise in government spending is slowed and taxpayer withholdings are increased, but that the deficit would still be 3.5 percent of GDP.
"At that, the reference values for the deficit criterium and the debt criterium set in the Maastricht Treaty will not be reached in 1997, based on data available today," the report said.
EMU participants will be required to reduce their overall outstanding debt to 60 percent of GDP.
